integrator_questions: With wheel_track at 0.14 m, does the controller need more kp to hold the bend response, or less kd to stop the signal from lagging? Compare the gain margin with the 0.12 m case.
Where does max_error occur now: on the oval's tightest bend (turn authority limit) or on the s-bend and slalom (damping)? This decides whether 0.14 m is past the optimum.
Does steering_oscillation fall relative to the 0.12 m run, and does control_effort rise or fall? Report whether line_loss_events change on the slalom.

intent: Single-variable test on the iteration 3 baseline (best score 69.18). Change only wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.14 m. Keep the 80 mm sensor row (contract maximum), 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch, 0.8 kg mass, 0.03 m wheels and 0.12 m body width. The track series so far is 0.10 m (scores 53.14 and 53.33) and 0.12 m (69.18), so a wider track is the next direction to test. Expected: steering oscillation stays near or below the 0.12 m value, s-bend and slalom progress rise, max_error approaches or drops below 0.060 m, and the score exceeds 69.18.
learning: Iterations 0 to 4 show two single-variable trends: sensor row forward position (monotone, 40 mm < 60 mm < 80 mm) and wheel track (0.10 m clearly worse than 0.12 m on the same row). Iteration 1 confounded mass, track, sensor size and pitch, so mass and sensor pitch remain untested in isolation. If 0.14 m beats 0.12 m, the optimum track lies above 0.12 m and the next single-variable test should be mass. If 0.14 m falls back, the optimum sits near 0.12 m and mass becomes the next test.
rationale: Scores by iteration: 0 (60 mm row, 0.12 m track) 65.96; 2 (40 mm row) 52.25; 3 (80 mm row) 69.18, the best so far; 4 (80 mm row, 0.10 m track) 53.14. Iteration 1 changed four variables at once and also used a 0.10 m track, and it scored 53.33. Two separate runs with the 0.10 m track both fell by about 16 points relative to the 0.12 m baseline, so narrowing the track is the strongest evidence so far. The authorized iteration 4 result shows the damage was concentrated on the s-bend (progress 0.156 to 0.081) and the slalom, with the oval less affected (progress 0.229 to 0.183). Steering oscillation on the s-bend also fell (0.148 to 0.067), so the narrow track looks sluggish or under-damped on the bends rather than oscillatory. Max error stays at 0.060 to 0.065 m on every track in every run, so the off-track limit is still the binding constraint. Lookahead is at its contract maximum (80 mm), so it cannot be pushed further. The next single-variable step is the other side of the track trend: widen wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.14 m (within the 0.18 m limit) and hold everything else at the iteration 3 values. A wider track lowers turn rate per unit wheel difference, which should damp the bend response, reduce the sluggish-to-overshoot swing, and keep the robot straighter at speed. I expect progress to rise on the s-bend and slalom relative to 0.12 m, with max error approaching or dropping below 0.060 m, and a score above 69.18. The risk is that a wider track lowers turn authority on the tightest bend, so max error could rise instead, which would show as a drop in oval progress.
